data.title: Could Skydance Be Bigger Than Disney? Skydance (NYSE:SKYD) Stock Rises
data.description:
Entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) could be bigger than Disney (DIS), or even bigger than Netflix (NFLX) thanks to its recently concluded merger deal. JPMorgan analysts actually gave Skydance stock an upgrade, taking it from Underweight to Neutral, though they also dialed back the price target. Skydance stock rose fractionally in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Skydance has seen a 53.41% loss in its share price over the past year.

Bigger Than You Might Expect

JPMorgan recently restarted coverage of Skydance, now that it is no longer either Paramount Skydance or Warner Bros. Discovery. The rating change was one thing, but JPMorgan lowered the price target from a previous level of $14 per share down to $9 per share.

The thesis behind this is that Skydance will see cost-saving opportunities as a result of the merger, as well as new opportunities to expand its presence in streaming. There will be more room for content monetization, as well as cross-selling of its streaming services, though the combination of the two services—HBO Max and Paramount+—may render that something of a moot point. Also, the combined firm will have the ability to remove some duplicated cost, though this may mean quite a few lost jobs.

Wiseman Out

Meanwhile Skydance will be operating on something like a back foot as the Paramount+ head of originals, Jane Wiseman, is leaving the company. It turns out that Wiseman's position may have been one of those "duplicated costs" we heard about previously. The new co-CEO and chief content officer for Skydance's direct-to-consumer operation, Casey Bloys, revealed that much of his original team from HBO will stay in their current positions.

Perhaps the most galling part of this is contained in Bloys' memo about the transition, where he said, "I also want to thank Jane Wiseman. Jane, in her partnership with Cindy Holland, has done amazing work at Paramount+. The development slate is incredibly impressive, and Jane has graciously offered to help with the transition. She is an extraordinarily talented executive. I appreciate all her support and wish her all the best." "Extraordinarily talented"…but not talented enough to keep, then?

Is Skydance a Good Stock to Buy Now?

data.title: Robinhood Stock (HOOD) Options Traders Are Pricing a 10.26% Earnings Swing
data.description:
Robinhood Markets (HOOD) is expected to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on October 27, 2026. The October 30, 2026 options expiration implies a 10.26%, or $9.75, move in either direction. With shares trading at $95.05, the nearest strike is $95, where the call costs $5.10 and the put costs $4.65. Therefore:

  • ATM straddle = $5.10 + $4.65 = $9.75
  • Implied dollar move = $9.75
  • Implied percentage move = $9.75 ÷ $95.05 × 100 = 10.26%
  • Upper bound = $95.05 + $9.75 = $104.80
  • Lower bound = $95.05 − $9.75 = $85.30
data.author: Vince Condarcuri

data.title: Why Did Analysts Slash Bloom Energy Stock (BE) Price Targets Despite Praising Q3 Earnings Beats?
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) stock sank 11% on Friday after the company's Q3 earnings report acted as a catalyst for analyst price target cuts for BE shares.

Here's how some of the top-ranked analysts on TipRanks adjusted their BE stock price targets after earnings.

  • J.P. Morgan analyst Mark Strouse lowered his BE stock price target to $292 from $314 and maintained a Buy rating. His price target suggests a possible 50.52% upside for the shares.
  • Roth MKM Chip Moore cut his price target to $230 from $260 and stuck with a Hold rating. The analyst's new price target implies an 18.56% upside for the stock.
  • BTIG analyst Gregory Lewis reduced his price target to $250 from $295 and kept a Buy rating. This new price target represents a 28.87% upside for BE.

Analysts were cautious with Bloom Energy despite a strong earnings report. The company's adjusted EPS of 94 cents and revenue of $1.24 billion both easily surpassed Wall Street's estimates of 69 cents per share and $1.07 billion in revenue.

Promotion

High conviction on BE? Try Tradr's BEX or BEZ

Bloom Energy also updated its 2026 guidance ranges to adjusted EPS of $3.10 to $3.40 and revenue of $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. At midpoints of $3.25 per share and revenue of $4.5 billion, the company is on track to smash analysts' estimates of $3.14 per share and revenue of $4.38 billion.

So What's Behind the BE Stock Price Target Cuts Today?

While J.P. Morgan analyst Strouse said that Bloom Energy "continues to impress," he still cut his price target. However, the analyst said this had more to do with lower trading multiples in the company's peer group.

As for Roth MKM analyst Moore, he pointed to multiple contractions as the reason for his BE stock price cut. That's despite what the analyst called "another quarter of very impressive results."

Moving onto BTIG analyst Lewis, he highlighted near-term margin drag connected to the ramp of new production capacity and expedited customer timelines as reasons for his price cut. Even so, he noted that Bloom Energy is in the prime position to deliver behind-the-meter (BTM) generation capacity that is high in demand.

Where Does Wall Street Stand on BE Stock After Earnings?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus for Bloom Energy is Moderate Buy, based on 10 Buy and 10 Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average BE stock price target of $291.50, representing a potential 51.08% upside for the shares. (See BE Stock Forecast)

data.title: The Best Range in a Mustang Mach-E is in the Standard Version; Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Slides
data.description:
Normally, to get the best feature set out of a new vehicle, you have to buy the highest-end trim package. But at legacy automaker Ford (F), the Mustang Mach-E comes with an unexpected bonus in its standard edition: the best range. Ford shares slid nearly 3% in Friday afternoon's trading, and Ford has also seen a 13.73% loss in its share price over the past year.

An Unexpected Win for the Budget Buyer

Normally, the standard version of any car is the cheapest version, because it comes with the fewest options. But in the Mustang Mach-E's case, you actually get better range out of a standard edition than with any other. Base model Mustang Mach-Es are now equipped with a larger battery as part of the 2027 model year. This means greater range for the base models. Previously Select and Premium trims got a 73 kWh battery, which has since been removed, and that leaves only the 88 kWh pack as the only option. The Mach-E GT and Rally versions get a 91 kWh battery, just like they did before.

The improvements are actually fairly substantial. The 2026 model of the Mustang Mach-E with a small battery and rear-wheel drive got 260 miles of range. The all-wheel-drive version got 240. With the extended-range battery those figures increased to 320 miles and 300 miles. The Mach-E GT, meanwhile, only gets around 280 miles, reports note.

And the other time…and the other…up to the sixth time Ford tried, and failed, to kill the Raptor.

Ultimately, the Ford Raptor emerged from the ashes of the Ford Baja 1000, reports noted, and went on to deliver some exciting new possibilities for Ford. The Raptor delivered value as a pickup, and also as an off-roading platform, which made it a surprisingly versatile entrant into Ford's lineup. This was in spite of the fact that Ford almost killed the Raptor project on six separate occasions.

data.title: Moderna's Cancer Vaccine Earns Praise from Doctors amid Stock Selloff
data.description:
Biotech company Moderna (MRNA) saw its shares fall by as much as 25% on Thursday, October 22, despite positive results from a late-stage trial of its personalized cancer vaccine. The treatment, developed with pharmaceutical giant Merck (MRK), reduced the risk of melanoma returning or causing death by 42% when combined with Merck's Keytruda cancer drug. However, investors had hoped for even stronger results after Moderna stock surged by more than 500% earlier this year. Still, six melanoma specialists described the findings as an important advancement in treating the dangerous form of skin cancer, according to CNBC.

The trial involved 1,137 patients who had undergone surgery to remove their tumors. Some received Keytruda alone, while others also received Moderna's experimental vaccine.

After two years, 82.2% of patients who received both treatments were alive without their cancer returning. That compares with 70% of patients who received Keytruda alone.

The combination also reduced the risk of cancer spreading to distant organs or causing death by 38%.

Why Doctors Are More Optimistic than Investors

The vaccine works differently from traditional cancer treatments. Doctors first examine a patient's tumor to identify mutations that make their cancer unique. Moderna then uses that information to create a personalized vaccine that teaches the immune system to recognize the remaining cancer cells. Since Keytruda helps the immune system attack cancer, the vaccine could make the existing treatment more effective.

Still, investors had expected results closer to an earlier trial that showed a 49% reduction in the risk of recurrence or death after five years. However, the latest study involved patients with different risk levels, which makes direct comparisons more difficult. Doctors also noted that the vaccine's benefits appeared stronger after six months. An additional analysis found a 58% reduction in recurrence or death risk after that point.

For Moderna, the treatment could become an important new source of revenue as the company tries to reduce its dependence on COVID-19 vaccines. In fact, Moderna reported a net loss of approximately $800 million in the second quarter. CEO Stéphane Bancel said that the company is preparing its application for regulatory approval and hopes to bring the treatment to market in 2027.

However, researchers still need longer-term data to determine whether the vaccine helps patients live longer.

data.title: U.S. to Drop Tariffs on Some Canadian Goods: LULU, SHOP, RY
data.description:
Multiple media reports say the Trump administration is planning to drop some of its tariffs on Canadian goods ahead of the U.S. midterm congressional elections. Republican Senator Susan Collins of Maine said on social media that she has secured tariff exemptions on a variety of Canadian agricultural products ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms

"I am pleased to have secured additional tariff exemptions products crucial to Maine's agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers," wrote Collins. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."

Leading Canadian stocks such as Lululemon Athletica (LULU), Shopify (SHOP), and Royal Bank of Canada (RY) were rising on the afternoon of Oct. 23.

A New U.S.-Canada Trade Deal?

Shortly after Collins social media post, U.S. President Donald Trump said that Canada and America are close to reaching a new trade deal. Asked by reporters about Collins comments, Trump said during a scrum with the media that his administration is "very close" to a "very good" trade deal with Canada. The president added that: "Canada's working very hard to make a deal with us."

While there has been little news within Canada about a new trade deal with the U.S., news that some tariffs will be lifted on Canadian goods is being cheered by America's northern neighbor. trade negotiations between the two countries had ground to a halt in recent months after the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on many Canadian-made products in August. Canada responded with counter-tariffs.

The Impact on Canada's Economy

U.S. tariffs have had a negative impact on Canada's economy, leading to job losses, inflation, and a slowdown in growth. It has also caused a political rift between the longtime allies and led many Canadians to boycott American products in protest and refuse to travel to the U.S. for business or vacation.

The U.S. had imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian goods such as steel, aluminum and motor vehicle parts and supplies, putting stranglehold on Canada's manufacturing sector. The tariffs on Canadian goods have become an issue in the midterm elections, particularly in battleground states that border Canada, such as Maine and Michigan. Many Americans say that the tariffs on Canadian items have driven up prices and are hurting their wallets.

data.title: Video Game Stock Stories Roundup: The Biggest News Moving the Gaming Sector This Week
data.description:
Investors have plenty of video game stock market news to catch up on this week. Updates from several major players in the space, such as Electronic Arts, Sony (SONY), CD Projekt (OTGLY), and Konami (JP:9766), top this week's gaming news.

1. EA Shuts Down BioWare and Cancels the Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts announced that it is shutting down RPG developer BioWare after more than 30 years. This is part of larger cuts at the game publisher. The studio's closure also means the end of early work on the next Mass Effect game. These cuts came after the company was taken private in a $55 billion deal on Aug. 4, 2026.

2. Marvel's Wolverine Tops U.S. Game Sales

Sony (SONY) scored a big win with Marvel's Wolverine. The game topped the U.S. sales charts in September, based on data from Circana. It also posted the highest launch-month dollar sales for a Sony-published game since Helldivers 2 in February 2024. That's good news for Sony despite a bit of controversy after the game's release.

Promotion

3. PlayStation's 'Father' Weighs In on the Disc Debate

Ken Kutaragi, known as the "Father of PlayStation," weighed in on Sony's plans to end production of physical discs in 2028. He said he understands why players link discs with owning their games. Even so, he argued that keeping physical media may no longer make economic sense. This comes as supply chain issues have increased console prices.

4. Cyberpunk 2077 Gets a Surprise Update

CD Projekt released Update 2.5 for Cyberpunk 2077 on Oct. 22. The Edgerunners 2 Update is a free patch adds new items and features tied to the second Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime series. The update is now out on PC, PlayStation 5, and Microsoft's (MSFT) Xbox Series X|S. An update for Nintendo's (NTODY) Switch 2 is also in the works.

5. Konami Says Human Talent Still Matters More Than AI

Konami president Hideki Hayakawa has downplayed fears that generative AI will reshape game development anytime soon. He argued that easier access to game engines and user-made content has already lowered barriers for new creators, reducing concerns that a new wave of copycat games will threaten the company. The president said AI could help speed up development, but that talented people are still behind the games.

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Down Today, 10/23/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Dow Jones (DJIA) are trading lower on Friday and are down by 0.38% and 1.14%, respectively. The losses come amid heightening tensions in the Middle East that have sent Brent crude (BZ) oil prices to their highest levels since May.

While President Trump previously said the U.S. would hold off on striking Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, both countries have already begun preparations for a return to action. Furthermore, Mike Waltz, U.S. Ambassador to the UN, warned that the war could drag on for another year if the Iranians refuse to negotiate.

Higher Oil Prices Fuel Rate Hike Bets and Inflation Fears

Rising oil prices have also propped up interest rate hike expectations. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the October 28 Fed meeting are at 10.5%, nearly doubling from 5.5% a day ago. Higher rates are generally viewed as a negative for stocks because they increase borrowing costs and discourage spending.

data.title: Intel Got Its Waiver: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Gains
data.description:
Just three days ago, we got word that chip stock Intel (INTC) was looking for a waiver from the federal government that would allow it to continue using a set of robotic tools that it was already using in its factories. The waiver was granted late yesterday, reports noted, which comes as little surprise. Intel stock gained over 1.5% in Friday afternoon's trading, and Intel has seen a 123.33% rally in its share price over the past year.

They Really Needed Those Robots

The issue at hand was that Intel needed a set of robotic devices that would help it make chips. But, under certain sections of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) regulations, foreign-made advanced robotics were not always allowed in the United States. With the waiver, Intel can continue to use the devices that it already has in place.

The FCC ultimately granted a one-year waiver of its own rules in a bid to prevent what it described as "…potential disruptions in the availability of domestic semiconductor manufacturing services for Intel's customers." Intel cited the fact that there were few, if any, domestically-produced alternatives that would have met the necessary requirements to actually carry out the tasks Intel needed them to carry out. It likely did not hurt that the United States government is a 10% owner of Intel, and likely did not want to do anything that might have impacted its investment therein.

The Next Trillion-Dollar Company?

Meanwhile, David Tykocinski—co-chief investment officer of Maverick Capital—has high hopes for Intel stock, believing that Intel could ultimately become the next trillion-dollar company. Tykocinski's projections are nothing new, but his making them serves as one more brick in a growing wall of credibility for Intel.

Basically his projections suggest that the rise of agentic AI is going to help Intel, because agentic AI depends heavily on central processing unit (CPU) chips. This rise will not solely help Intel, but will rather help other companies in the field that also specialize in CPUs. Intel's lead in the CPU space, however, may mean this development will help it more than others. This means that Intel has an upside of over 100% earnings growth in the next couple of years, reports noted.
